stories.headline: AMD posts record $11.5B quarter as data center revenue doubles; shares fall on guidance

key_facts.fact: AMD reported Q2 2026 revenue of $11.5 billion on August 4, up 50% year over year, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.38 and non-GAAP EPS of $1.66.
key_facts.excerpt: Second quarter revenue was $11.5 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.0 billion, net income was $2.3 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.38. On a non-GAAP basis... diluted earnings per share was $1.66.

key_facts.fact: Data Center segment revenue hit a record $6.7 billion, up 107% year over year, and made up 58% of company revenue versus 42% a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center segment revenue was $6.7 billion, up 107% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPUs.

key_facts.fact: AMD guided to about $13 billion in Q3 revenue, plus or minus $300 million, roughly 41% annual growth, above the $12.52 billion consensus but below the $14 billion some analysts wanted.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD said it expects about $13 billion in revenue for the current quarter, plus or minus $300 million, versus LSEG expectations of $12.52 billion. Some analysts had been looking for guidance as high as $14 billion.

key_facts.fact: On the call, CEO Lisa Su said data center revenue should grow 'well over 100%' in 2027 and that 'your data center AI number is probably too low'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I think what you're hearing from us is that your data center AI number is probably too low... I think this notion of over 100% should consider be well over 100%."

key_facts.fact: AMD's release cites a strategic partnership with Anthropic covering deployment of up to two gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs in Helios rack-scale systems; Su named OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic as the three anchor customers.
key_facts.excerpt: the strategic partnership with Anthropic and the deployment of up to two gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs in AMD Helios rack-scale solutions and multiyear collaboration

key_facts.fact: Helios starts shipping late in Q3 with a step-up in Q4, and AMD says server revenue will grow more than 80% year over year in the second half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: server revenue in 2H26 to grow >80% YoY; in 2027, off a higher base, grow >70% YoY... Helios starts shipping late Q3 and is much larger in Q4.

key_facts.fact: AMD shares fell around 6-8% in after-hours trading despite the beat, with the stock up nearly 130% year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the beat, AMD stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading.

stories.headline: Anthropic confirms it is building an in-house silicon team to design custom chips for Claude

key_facts.fact: An Anthropic spokesperson confirmed to Business Insider that the company is assembling an internal silicon team to design chips for Claude, the first public confirmation after months of reports.
key_facts.excerpt: An Anthropic spokesman told Business Insider that the firm is working on putting together an internal silicon team to design chips for Claude... the firm has finally confirmed its intentions publicly for the first time.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is hiring engineers for a 'custom silicon team' who have taken semiconductor designs from concept to production, with pay in the $330,000-$485,000 range.
key_facts.excerpt: the company is hiring engineers for a "custom silicon team". The requirement is that the engineer must have experience of moving semiconductor designs from concept to production... pays between $330,000 [and] $485,000.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says its own chips are not meant to replace existing suppliers: it will keep using AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD hardware alongside anything it designs.
key_facts.excerpt: its own chips are not meant to replace those partners. Instead, the company says it will continue using hardware from AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD alongside any future chips it designs itself.

key_facts.fact: The effort is being led by Clive Chan, an engineer who worked on OpenAI's custom chip team, according to reports on the Business Insider story.
key_facts.excerpt: Previously, Anthropic explored the possibility of creating its own AI chips and has now progressed to team-building, with Clive Chan, an OpenAI chip veteran, spearheading the initiative.

key_facts.fact: Reuters previously reported Anthropic was exploring its own chips and The Information reported manufacturing talks with Samsung Electronics; neither company has confirmed a partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters also reported that Anthropic was considering working with Samsung to manufacture the chips, although neither company has officially confirmed such a partnership.

key_facts.fact: In April Anthropic signed a deal with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity coming online from 2027, its largest compute commitment to date.
key_facts.excerpt: We have signed a new agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that we expect to come online starting in 2027.

stories.headline: Samsung unveils zHBM, memory stacked on top of AI chips, and a 400-layer NAND at FMS 2026

key_facts.fact: At Future of Memory and Storage 2026 in Santa Clara on August 4, Samsung previewed concept models of zHBM and zNAND-O and introduced V10 BV-NAND with more than 400 layers.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung presented its latest AI memory portfolio and technology roadmap, including a preview of its zHBM and zNAND-O concept models, the industry-first introduction of its V10 BV-NAND with 400-plus layers.

key_facts.fact: zHBM stacks high-bandwidth memory vertically on top of the AI accelerator instead of beside it, and Samsung says a next-generation interface using zHBM delivers roughly eight times the performance of HBM5.
key_facts.excerpt: zHBM presents a new memory architecture that vertically stacks HBM directly above AI accelerators... A next-generation interface system incorporating zHBM is expected to deliver approximately eight times the performance of HBM5.

key_facts.fact: Using wafer bonding, zHBM is designed to reach more than 10 times the memory density of HBM5, triple the energy efficiency and cut thermal resistance by more than half.
key_facts.excerpt: zHBM can achieve more than 10 times the memory density of HBM5 while enhancing energy efficiency threefold and reducing thermal resistance by more than half.

key_facts.fact: V10 BV-NAND uses wafer bonding to stack cells and circuits separately, raising memory density about 58% over the previous V9 generation, 13 years after Samsung introduced V-NAND at the same conference.
key_facts.excerpt: Compared with the previous-generation V9, memory density has increased by approximately 58%, while read/write performance and I/O speed have also improved.

key_facts.fact: Samsung DRAM development head Kim Kyung-ryun said the company will implement gate-all-around transistors in HBM for the first time and use a 2nm foundry process, declaring 'Samsung is back'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We will overcome this barrier by implementing gate-all-around (GAA) transistors in HBM for the first time and introducing a 2nm... ultra-fine foundry process." ... Kim also expressed confidence, remarking, "Samsung is back."

key_facts.fact: Samsung plans to ramp HBM4 production in the second half of 2026 and has not given a definitive timeline for HBM5 or zHBM, as it fights SK Hynix and Micron in a near-$1 trillion memory market.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung intends to ramp up production of HBM4 in the second half of this year. It hasn't yet offered a definitive timeline for HBM5 or this future technology.

stories.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix tested Chinese AMEC etching tools as a hedge against US export curbs

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on August 5 that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have been evaluating chipmaking equipment from Shanghai-based AMEC for possible use at their Chinese factories, citing three people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are evaluating chipmaking equipment from China's Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment (AMEC) for possible use at their Chinese factories, three people familiar with the matter said.

key_facts.fact: The testing of AMEC etching equipment began about two years ago, when it was unclear whether Washington would keep allowing US chipmaking tools into China.
key_facts.excerpt: The memory chipmakers began testing AMEC etching equipment about two years ago, when uncertainty was mounting over whether Washington would continue allowing them to import U.S. chipmaking tools into China.

key_facts.fact: Samsung told Reuters it has not tested AMEC equipment for use at its China factory and had not considered doing so; SK Hynix declined to comment and AMEC did not respond.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung said in a statement to Reuters that it has not tested AMEC equipment for use at its China factory and had not considered doing so. SK Hynix declined to comment.

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department gave the two firms' China fabs validated end user status in 2023, revoked it in 2025, then granted annual import licences for 2026; the companies fear future curbs could extend to servicing and replacing installed Western tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington revoked the VEU authorization in 2025 and later granted an annual license... both companies remain wary that future restrictions could extend beyond new equipment to the servicing, repair or replacement of Western tools already installed.

key_facts.fact: Samsung runs a NAND plant in Xian and SK Hynix has NAND in Dalian and DRAM in Wuxi, all heavily dependent on etching tools from Applied Materials and Lam Research.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung operates its NAND flash memory chip plant in Xian, and SK Hynix has NAND facilities in Dalian and a DRAM memory chip plant in Wuxi. Their China factories rely heavily on etching tools supplied by U.S. firms including Applied Materials and Lam Research.

key_facts.fact: Separately, on August 4 AMEC guided to first-half revenue of Rmb 6.691bn ($984m), up 34.89%, with net profit up 282% to 311%.
key_facts.excerpt: On August 4, AMEC separately guided to first-half revenue of Rmb 6.691bn($984m), up 34.89%, and net profit up between 282% and 311%.

stories.headline: SpaceX and Nvidia to build Starmind AI1 orbital compute payload; Musk commits to Nvidia GPUs only

key_facts.fact: SpaceX announced on August 4 that it is partnering with Nvidia to design the compute payload of the Starmind AI1 satellite, with each Starmind satellite carrying Nvidia Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs for datacenter-class space compute.
key_facts.excerpt: "SpaceX is partnering with @Nvidia to design the Starmind AI1 satellite compute payload. Each of the Starmind satellites will include NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs for datacenter-class space compute," SpaceX said in a post on X.

key_facts.fact: Prototype testing of the Starmind AI1 satellite is scheduled for early 2027, with mass production planned for later that year if development stays on schedule.
key_facts.excerpt: Prototype testing for the Starmind AI1 satellite is scheduled for early 2027. SpaceX expects mass production to begin later that year if development stays on schedule.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia says its Space-1 Vera Rubin module delivers up to 25 times the AI processing performance of an H100 GPU, with commercial shipments expected to start later this year.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Nvidia, its Space-1 Vera Rubin module can deliver up to 25 times the AI processing performance of an H100 GPU. Commercial shipments of the platform are expected to begin later this year.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk said the same day that SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively 'because they are the best'; Nvidia shares rose about 3% and SpaceX stock nearly 9%.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk also endorsed the partnership, saying SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively because "they are the best." ... Nvidia shares gained about 3% during Tuesday trading, while SpaceX stock climbed nearly 9%.

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call Musk said Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 racks will power SpaceX data centers, with about 2GW of compute installed by the end of 2026 and 10GW by the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Initially, a total of 2GW of compute capacity will be installed by this year's end, and a total of 10 GW of capacity is expected to come online by the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's infrastructure already includes more than 220,000 Nvidia GPUs, according to reporting on Musk's announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent data indicates that SpaceX's infrastructure already includes over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs, reflecting significant investment in NVIDIA's technology for large-scale AI applications.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia introduced its space computing platform in March naming six launch partners without SpaceX; Tuesday's announcement adds SpaceX to that ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: When Nvidia introduced its space platform in March, it named six launch partners but did not include SpaceX. Tuesday's announcement adds the aerospace company to that ecosystem.

stories.headline: Citic values Unitree above $7.4B ahead of Shanghai IPO, China's first pure humanoid robot listing

key_facts.fact: Citic Securities, the IPO sponsor, told investors in a report seen by Reuters on August 4 that Unitree Technology should be worth 50.6 billion to 55.9 billion yuan ($7.4 billion or more) six to 12 months after listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Citic Securities expected the Hangzhou-based company to be worth 50.6 billion to 55.9 billion yuan six to 12 months after listing later this month. The valuation report, distributed to investors and seen by Reuters, is largely seen as guidance ahead of Wednesday's IPO price enquiry.

key_facts.fact: The report values Unitree at roughly 20 times expected 2026 sales and about 80 times forecast earnings; the company aims to raise 4.2 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Citic Securities' report values Unitree roughly 20 times this year's expected sales, and about 80 times forecast earnings... aims to raise 4.2 billion yuan to fund innovation and production.

key_facts.fact: Unitree guided to first-half 2026 revenue of about 1.1 billion yuan ($156 million), up 35.6% to 45.4% year over year, a sharp deceleration from 332% growth a year earlier, with adjusted net profit down 6% to 22%.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expects first-half revenue of about CNY1.1 billion ($156 million), representing year-on-year growth of between 35.6 percent and 45.4 percent.

key_facts.fact: Unitree will issue 40.45 million shares, 10% of post-offering capital, with preliminary price inquiry on August 5, pricing on August 6 and subscriptions on August 10; Citic is sponsor and lead underwriter.
key_facts.excerpt: Preliminary pricing inquiries will take place on August 5, 2026. Offline and online subscriptions are set to begin simultaneously on August 10... Unitree plans to issue 40.45 million shares in this IPO, representing 10% of the post-offering capital.

key_facts.fact: Unitree shipped more than 5,500 humanoid robots in 2025, more than any other company, on revenue of 1.699 billion yuan with a 60% gross margin on core businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, Unitree shipped over 5,500 humanoid robots — more than any other company globally... Annual revenue reached 1.699 billion yuan, with a gross margin of 60.13% on core businesses.

key_facts.fact: The listing comes after Washington added foreign-made advanced robots to the FCC Covered List, restricting the equipment authorisation needed for US sales, and after the US added Unitree in June to a list of firms it says aid Beijing's military.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington recently added foreign-made advanced robots to its Covered List, restricting their ability to obtain the equipment authorisation required for U.S. sales. In June, the US added Unitree and other major Chinese tech firms to a list of companies it believes are aiding Beijing's military.

stories.headline: Exclaim Robotics leaves stealth with $4.95M to build robots that repair AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Zurich-based Exclaim Robotics came out of stealth on August 4 with a $4.95 million (EUR 4.29 million) pre-seed round co-led by Founderful and Playfair.
key_facts.excerpt: Exclaim Robotics, a Zürich-based startup building robots to maintain AI data centres, has exited stealth mode with a €4.29 million ($4.95 million) pre-Seed round co-led by Founderful and Playfair.

key_facts.fact: The company is building autonomous mobile robots that carry out routine repair and maintenance work inside AI data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is building autonomous mobile robots that perform routine repair and maintenance work inside AI data centres.

key_facts.fact: The startup will be led by veteran roboticist Helen Oleynikova and targets hyperscale data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Veteran roboticist Helen Oleynikova will lead startup, which will develop repair robots for hyperscale data centres

key_facts.fact: The capital will fund first prototypes, robotics hardware purchases and hiring of robotics and hardware engineers in Zurich.
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans to use this capital to build its first prototypes, acquire robotics hardware, and grow the engineering team. It is currently hiring robotics and hardware engineers in Zürich.
